title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is shared by every instance on the machine; a second instance is offered another run's live sequence and cannot dismiss the prompt
summary: Already closed by an earlier wave in this working tree, cause and all. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart no longer passes the bare application-support root to sequencerSetCheckpointDir: resolveGuiCheckpointDirectory() (app_shell.dart:82-89) derives <database dir>/checkpoints from resolveDefaultDatabaseFile, which honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/database/connection.dart:12-25), so two instances pointed at different data dirs can no longer see each other's checkpoint. adoptLegacyGuiCheckpoint carries a pre-upgrade file forward only when no override is set. The dialog's missing escape is also closed: buildCheckpointRecoveryDialog gained a 'Not now' action that appears once an attempt has failed. The verifier had already REFUTED the re-prompt-loop half of the finding (runAppCheckpointRecovery only loops when resume/discard throws).
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/checkpoint_directory_test.dart (4 tests, all green; drives the real AppShell so cutting the call site fails them)
revert_check: Not re-reverted by me - the fix and its test predate this wave. Verified green: flutter test test/screens/shell/checkpoint_directory_test.dart -> 4/4 pass, and the first test asserts backend.checkpointDir == '<databaseRoot>/checkpoints' and isNot(support.path).
caveats: The verifier corrected this to P3 because production installs take a per-data-dir single-instance lock. A concurrent agent additionally re-anchored the headless host's resolveHostCheckpointDirectory on resolveSkotiqDataDirectory during this session.

title: A rig with no filter wheel cannot create any integration goal, so the autopilot can never be given a target
summary: Both halves are closed in this working tree. UI: integration_goals_editor.dart gates the refusal on wheelOnlineWithNoSlots (a wheel that IS connected and reports zero slots) instead of availableFilters.isEmpty, so a wheel-less rig gets one 'No filter' slot carrying smartNightUnfilteredName. Core - the half the previous agent listed as needs_shared_change - is also done: SchedulerCandidateLoader._availableFilters (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart:554-571) now returns smartNightPlanningFilters(profile.filterNames), so a wheel-less profile yields [''] and the engine's filter-containment checks, scoring and buildSequenceForCandidate all admit the unfiltered goal.
revert_check: Not re-reverted by me. Verified green: flutter test test/providers/scheduler_project_filter_test.dart -> 7/7 pass, including 'a profile with no filters is loaded as one unfiltered slot, not none', which asserts candidate.availableFilters == [''] AND that the operator's 20 x 180 s unfiltered goal survives into engine.buildSequenceForCandidate rather than being replaced by the defensive 30 s frame.

title: False "Rises late" warning on a target that is up all night, and the same card gives two different rise times
summary: Two causes, both removed. (a) The warning no longer reads visibility.riseTime. scoreTargetForNight already walks the night at 15-minute steps against the skyline-aware effective minimum; it now records the FIRST sample that clears it (firstObservableTime) and _generateNightWarnings gates on that. A target that is usable at nightStart produces no warning at all, and one that only becomes usable in the last third says 'Usable only from HH:MM' - the instant it clears the configured minimum, not a geometric horizon crossing it cannot image at. (b) AltitudeChart stopped solving rise/transit/set against the raw wall clock: it anchors on AstronomyCalculations.nightDateOf of the midpoint of the window it is PLOTTING, the same rule TargetScoringService uses, so one card cannot print two rise times for one event.
revert_check: (a) Restored HEAD's rise-time block verbatim over the new one in target_scoring.dart (the `if (visibility.riseTime != null && peakAlt >= 0)` gate emitting 'Rises late at ...'): BOTH planetarium tests failed - 'Expected: empty / Actual: WhereIterable<TargetWarning>:[Instance of TargetWarning]' on the up-all-night target, and the late-riser message assertion. Restored, both pass. (b) Changed altitude_chart.dart:236 back to `date: now,`: the widget test failed with Expected '12:01' / Actual '11:54' - the exact pair of rise times the finding reported on one card. Restored, passes.
caveats: The M92/2026-08-01 case in the report no longer reproduces on its own because an earlier wave's nightDateOf anchoring moved the scorer onto the same day as the chart; the defect class is still live and the test locates a qualifying sky at runtime (searched, not hard-coded, because calculateObjectVisibility anchors on LOCAL noon - verified green under TZ=America/New_York, UTC, Asia/Tokyo and Europe/Berlin). Full planetarium suite: 474 pass, 1 fail = test/benchmark/golden_compare_test.dart, which is @Tags(['golden']), host-specific and excluded from `melos run test`.

title: Observing Alerts refresh is a silent no-op and the screen can never show anything
summary: The AAVSO source is gone, because it could never have worked. I re-verified the endpoint live: https://vsx.aavso.org/index.php?view=api.list&format=json&maxrec=5 returns exactly {"VSXObjects":[]}, while the same url WITH a cone (ra/dec/radius) returns rows - api.list is a positional catalog search, and VSX has no 'recent alerts' selector; six candidate aavso.org alert-notice feeds all 404. The parser could not have read a real answer either: VSX wraps rows as {"VSXObjects":{"VSXObject":[...]}} (the code requires a List), returns RA2000 in decimal DEGREES (the shared _parseRaString treats a bare decimal as HOURS and rejects >= 24), and names the classification VariabilityType, not Type. So: kFetchableTransientSources now lives beside TransientSource and contains only tns; getAllAlerts no longer dispatches AAVSO; TransientAlertSettings.enabledSources defaults to {tns, manual} instead of {aavso, mpec, cbat, manual}; and the sheet renders AAVSO alongside MPEC/CBAT as 'AAVSO - not available', with copy naming TNS as the one feed and Settings > Science as where its bot credentials live. Combined with the per-source status strip an earlier wave added, a default install now reads 'TNS: skipped - no API key' (actionable) instead of either a permanent red VSX error or 'AAVSO: 0 alerts, checked 23:14' - a dead feed reported as a quiet sky.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/transient_alert_service_test.dart ('an AAVSO source that is enabled is never fetched', 'the shipped default enables only feeds that are fetched'); packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/transients_source_honesty_test.dart ('AAVSO, MPEC and CBAT are never rendered as monitored sources', 'a rig with only unavailable sources enabled is told none is being checked')
revert_check: Three separate reverts, each of a distinct production call site. (1) Re-added the AAVSO dispatch to getAllAlerts (a _fetchOutcome that GETs the old VSX url): 'an AAVSO source that is enabled is never fetched' failed on verifyNever(mockHttpClient.get). (2) Set kFetchableTransientSources back to {tns, aavso}: BOTH app tests failed - the 'AAVSO - not available' chip and the 'No alert source is enabled' strip. (3) Put the old {aavso, mpec, cbat, manual} default back into the generated TransientAlertSettings constructor: 'the shipped default enables only feeds that are fetched' failed ('Expected: empty / Actual: Set:[...]'). All three restored; 25 core + 8 app transient tests pass.
caveats: This removes a source rather than repairing it, deliberately: there is no URL at VSX that answers 'what transients are there tonight', so 'point AAVSO at a working query' (the report's proposed fix) is not achievable. TNS remains fully implemented against the real Search/Get wire contract and is reachable from Settings > Science, so the surface can show rows - but an operator with no TNS bot still sees an empty (now honestly labelled) screen. The AAVSO-shaped fixtures in transient_alert_service_test.dart were rewritten onto TNS payloads, which also means the caching/filtering/coordinate-parsing coverage now runs against a response shape the upstream actually produces. Regenerating freezed for the changed default also picked up other agents' in-flight model edits in skotiq_core (app_settings, weather_status, phd2_models). One existing core test needed updating: transient_alert_persistence_test's 'rapid independent settings edits merge into the persisted snapshot' toggled TNS expecting it to turn ON; TNS is now on by default, so the toggle turns it off - the assertion was inverted and the merge behaviour it actually tests is unchanged. Suites: skotiq_core transient+science+scheduler subset 257/257 (every core file I touched, plus its consumers); skotiq_app screens/transients 8/8 and screens/{transients,suggestions,framing} 150/150; apps/desktop transient_handlers 4/4. The full skotiq_core run finished 5385 pass / 9 fail, and the failures visible in its log (flat_wizard_config_lifecycle, weather_safety_nothing_to_safe x2, nina_sequence_fidelity) are all in files other agents are editing concurrently, not in any file this fix touches.

title: Night Outlook hero card freezes its "Alt" and "Airmass" readouts while the list card for the same object keeps updating
summary: Already closed by an earlier wave in this working tree, at the place the verifier corrected the finding to (screens/framing/altitude_chart.dart, not _primary_target_card.dart). _AltitudeChartState now holds a Timer.periodic(1 minute) started in initState and cancelled in dispose that calls _refreshCurrentPosition(), which re-solves only the present-tense altitude/airmass against widget.nowValue() (and falls back to a full _calculateData when the clock has left the plotted window). The verifier's note that 'the ticker the proposed fix points at does not exist' is now moot - one was added.
revert_check: Not re-reverted by me. Verified green alongside the checkpoint test: the first case pumps the chart at a fixed instant, advances the injected clock and the tester by 20 minutes with no rebuild/scroll/ra-dec change, and asserts the 'Alt: ' and 'Airmass: ' chip values are isNot the mount-time values; a second case asserts the timer is cancelled on unmount (flutter_test fails the test itself on a surviving timer).
caveats: The verifier also corrected the finding's premise that the candidate-list card 'keeps updating' - it uses the same widget and only appeared to, because scrolling recycled it through initState. Both now track the clock for the same reason.
